metadata.framework: ansible (in-house CLI/plugin automation framework; not a web framework)
notes: Labeling performed by glm-5.3 running as the Claude Code CLI agent (lead) plus 8 fork subagents of the same model; every judgment is LLM-authored against the real source tree at dataset/codeql_databases/ansible_vuln (read-only).
Deterministic single-pass judgment; no sampling temperature applies (CLI agent reasoning, not a temperature-sampled API completion).
Scope: Pass 2 restricted to CWE-78 (OS command injection) per user request. Pass 1 is a schema-compatibility placeholder with empty entries, per user instruction.

labels_raw_pass2.json contains all 1665 per-candidate-row labels (1249 source rows + 416 sink rows from iris/extraction/*.csv, none skipped); labels.json contains the deduplicated signature-level view.
One sanitizer entry (shlex_quote) was added from LLM source reading rather than the candidate CSVs; evidence: lib/ansible/module_utils/basic.py:1915-1916, lib/ansible/plugins/action/__init__.py:1037.

Batches: S1 module_params (561), S2 cli_args (363), S3 task_args/env/stdin (283), S4 remote/deserialized (42), K1 run_command (323), K2 subprocess (38), K3 action/connection layer (40), K4 pexpect/wrappers (15). Per-batch judgment files: iris/labels/_work/out_*.jsonl; rubric: iris/labels/_work/rubric.md.
PyVul ground truth and fix commits were not consulted; source tree and databases unmodified.

entries.rationale: TerminalBase._exec_cli_command(self, cmd) at terminal/__init__.py:68 passes cmd (param 1) directly to self._connection.exec_command(cmd) at line 74 — direct param passthrough into the exec-family protocol; taint crossing this wrapper reaches remote device execution.

Call self._connection.exec_command(cmd) inside _exec_cli_command: arg0 cmd is the remote network-device CLI command string; network modules build it from module params and it is executed on the device via the persistent connection. Remote shell semantics (CWE-78).

NetworkConnectionBase.exec_command(self, cmd, in_data, sudoable) (def at connection/__init__.py:271; CSV row says 304 — line offset) passes cmd (param 1) to self._local.exec_command(cmd, in_data, sudoable) at 272, which reaches local.py Popen execution. Key flow step for network connection command taint.
evidence: lib/ansible/plugins/connection/__init__.py:271-272 — def exec_command(self, cmd, in_data=None, sudoable=True): return self._local.exec_command(cmd, in_data, sudoable)
CSV location 304 does not match; actual def verified at 271

entries.rationale: NetworkConnectionBase.exec_command param in_data (index 2) flows only to the in_data (stdin payload) position of self._local.exec_command — never the command position; not a CWE-78-relevant flow step.
evidence: lib/ansible/plugins/connection/__init__.py:271-272 — in_data passed as arg 1 (stdin), not arg 0 (cmd)

entries.rationale: NetworkConnectionBase.exec_command param sudoable (index 3) is a boolean privilege-escalation flag forwarded positionally; never part of a command string.

self._local.exec_command(cmd, in_data, sudoable) at connection/__init__.py:272 (CSV row says 305 — line offset): arg0 cmd is delegated to the local connection executor (local.py:64-105 Popen with shell=isinstance(cmd, str)); network-CLI commands execute here.

cli/__init__.py:421 in CLI.pager(): Popen('less --version', shell=True) — arg0 is a fixed string literal, no attacker-influenced component reaches this shell execution. Shell semantics present but no input flow.
evidence: lib/ansible/cli/__init__.py:421 — p = subprocess.Popen('less --version', shell=True, ...) literal command

entries.rationale: CLI.pager_pipe(text, cmd) passes its cmd parameter (arg index 1) directly to subprocess.Popen(cmd, shell=True) at cli/__init__.py:439 — the function is both the wrapper edge and the shell execution point. Callers pass os.environ['PAGER'] (cli/__init__.py:421) or literal 'less' (cli/__init__.py:434), so the local admin's PAGER env var flows unquoted into a shell; CWE-78 semantics with local-admin trust level.
evidence: lib/ansible/cli/__init__.py:439 — cmd = subprocess.Popen(cmd, shell=True, stdin=subprocess.PIPE, stdout=sys.stdout)
lib/ansible/cli/__init__.py:421 — CLI.pager_pipe(text, os.environ['PAGER']) caller passes PAGER env value

entries.rationale: cli/__init__.py:434 in CLI.pager_pipe(): Popen(cmd, shell=True) where cmd is os.environ['PAGER'] passed from pager() at line 419 (or 'less'). Genuine shell=True execution of an environment-sourced string — CWE-78 semantics; trust level is local-admin environment (the process owner controls it anyway), so tp-semantics with reduced confidence.
evidence: lib/ansible/cli/__init__.py:419 — CLI.pager_pipe(text, os.environ['PAGER']) supplies cmd from env

entries.rationale: _remote_file_exists: cmd = self._connection._shell.exists(path) then _low_level_execute_command(cmd=cmd, sudoable=True); path comes from action callers (task/module paths), and the shell plugin interpolates it into a remote test command. Remote shell execution of arg0.

Temporary-directory creation: cmd = self._connection._shell.mkdtemp(basefile=..., system=..., tmpdir=tmpdir) executed via _low_level_execute_command; tmpdir derives from the remote_tmp shell option (config/vars, admin-level) and basefile is a generated temp name. Remote shell exec; taint plausibility moderate.

Temp-dir cleanup: cmd = self._connection._shell.remove(tmp_path, recurse=True) executed via _low_level_execute_command; tmp_path is the shell plugin's internal tmpdir. Remote shell exec of arg0; inputs are controller-internal paths.
evidence: lib/ansible/plugins/action/__init__.py:452-453 — cmd = shell.remove(tmp_path, recurse=True); tmp_rm_res = self._low_level_execute_command(cmd, sudoable=False)

entries.rationale: _remote_chmod: cmd = self._connection._shell.chmod(paths, mode) executed via _low_level_execute_command; paths arrive from action callers (remote file paths derived from task/module args). Remote shell execution of arg0.
evidence: lib/ansible/plugins/action/__init__.py:729-730 — cmd = shell.chmod(paths, mode); res = self._low_level_execute_command(cmd, sudoable=sudoable)

entries.rationale: _remote_chown: cmd = self._connection._shell.chown(paths, user) executed remotely; user is become_user/task-sourced, paths from action callers. Remote shell execution of arg0.
evidence: lib/ansible/plugins/action/__init__.py:737-738 — cmd = shell.chown(paths, user); res = self._low_level_execute_command(cmd, sudoable=sudoable)

entries.rationale: _remote_chgrp: cmd = self._connection._shell.chgrp(paths, group) executed remotely via _low_level_execute_command; group/paths from action callers and task vars. Remote shell execution of arg0.
evidence: lib/ansible/plugins/action/__init__.py:745-746 — cmd = shell.chgrp(paths, group); res = self._low_level_execute_command(cmd, sudoable=sudoable)

entries.rationale: _remote_set_user_facl: cmd = self._connection._shell.set_user_facl(paths, user, mode) executed remotely; arguments from action callers. Remote shell execution of arg0.
evidence: lib/ansible/plugins/action/__init__.py:753-754 — cmd = shell.set_user_facl(paths, user, mode); res = self._low_level_execute_command(cmd, sudoable=sudoable)

entries.rationale: Remote user expansion: cmd = self._connection._shell.expand_user(expand_path) where expand_path = '~%s' % (become_user or remote_user); users come from become config/play vars. Remote shell execution of arg0, moderate taint plausibility.

Fallback pwd probe: cmd = self._connection._shell.pwd() is a fixed constant command with no data flowing into it; the call is a genuine remote shell execution point (sink semantics) but no taint is plausible, so the label is a false positive for finding purposes.
evidence: lib/ansible/plugins/action/__init__.py:863 — pwd = self._low_level_execute_command(cmd, sudoable=False).get('stdout') with cmd = shell.pwd() (constant)

entries.rationale: Module execution in _execute_module: cmd = self._connection._shell.build_module_command(environment_string, shebang, cmd, arg_path=...) built from interpreter/module path and task-sourced module args, then _low_level_execute_command(cmd, sudoable, in_data) executes it on the target. This is the main controller-side module-launch shell sink.
